source: Constructed demo source, NOT a ScreenCaptureKit capture and NOT FRAMEFLOW_CAPTURE_SYNTHETIC: the repo's own demo page tests/demo-app/index.html ("Acme Dashboard", the page the author's real capture docs/media/sample-real-capture-demo-page.mp4 shows) rendered in an Electron window at 2x, one screenshot per 1/30 s of virtual time (2400x1500, 16.5 s), with scripted pointer input sent through CDP and logged as a FrameFlow cursor.json (60 Hz samples + 6 clicks). Project built with the repo's createProject() exactly like tests/e2e/helpers.ts openDemoProject (recorded-style project with cursor telemetry, Calm feel, Editorial, Halo). The real sample capture was not usable as a source: it is already a composed export and has no cursor.json.
app_build: electron-vite production build in out/ (npm run build at a96eb18, unpackaged), launched by Playwright _electron with FRAMEFLOW_TEST=1 and isolated userData/library like tests/e2e/helpers.ts launch()
capture_method: CDP Page.startScreencast (JPEG q95, 2880x1800 device pixels of the 1440x900 window at forced device-scale-factor 2) on the FrameFlow main window, plus page.screenshot stills after export finished; UI driven by Playwright CDP mouse/keyboard (the OS mouse was never moved). Assembled with ffmpeg: kept ranges of the capture timeline (idle waits and the middle ~3 s of the export progress cut), UI played back at 1.2x capture speed, then the export slice appended (scaled to 1600x900, padded to 16:10 with #0e0e14 bars).
crop: full app window content (no OS chrome), 2880x1800 -> 1600x1000 lanczos; export slice letterboxed
notes: A capture-only pointer marker (22 px grey ring, pointer-events:none, injected into the page DOM only during capture) shows where the CDP pointer is, because CDP input has no OS cursor. It is not part of FrameFlow. The arrow cursor with the halo INSIDE the preview/export is FrameFlow's own rendered cursor from cursor.json. Segment ranges (s of capture): [[0.29,5.49],[5.49,12.35],[12.35,17.45],[17.45,23.88],[27.28,30.05]]. CRF 23, no audio track.
